Town hall stories

Ten people who keep a small town running, one comic each. The same winter roads contract runs through every story, seen from a different desk.

Donna · Town ClerkMarc · Finance DirectorSheila · Executive Administrative AssistantTom · Town ManagerLinda · Treasurer and Tax CollectorRay · Purchasing OfficerKaren · Budget Committee ChairPriya · Deputy Finance Director, Accounts PayableOkafor · Independent AuditorDave · IT Coordinator and Records Manager
Story 1 of 10 · Town Clerk

Give me back my Tuesday

Donna, Town Clerk. Elected, 18 years in the office.

JobAnswer residents accurately and fast, and never be the reason the town looks like it is hiding something.

1

Tuesday morning. The clerk's counter.

Sam, a residentI'd like everything the town has paid the plow company this winter.

DonnaLast year, that was a records request.

2

That meant pulling files, writing a letter, and a wait of about three weeks.

3

This year, the answer is already public.

DonnaIt's on the town's records page. No account, no form.

4

The contract, the award and every payment, against the winter roads line.

Budgeted$120,000
Committed$48,000
Paid so far$16,200
5

She sends Sam the link instead of a form letter.

DonnaHere's the page. You can download the files, too.

6

And if a published number is ever wrong?

DonnaWe publish a corrected version that links to the original. Both stay on record.

7

One click checks each file against its fingerprint on a public blockchain.

Matches what the town published

Sam, a residentSo nobody changed it after the fact.

8

Tuesday afternoon.

DonnaNo records request this time. I got my Tuesday back.

A link instead of a records request. Back to the list

Story 2 of 10 · Finance Director

Closing the month without a fire drill

Marc, Finance Director. Appointed, 6 years, the town's CFO in all but name.

JobKnow where every department stands against budget, and catch problems before the auditor or a councilor does.

1

Last day of the month. The finance office.

A select board memberAre winter roads over budget? People say the plow company is running up charges.

MarcGive me ten minutes.

2

He used to rebuild that answer by hand, in a spreadsheet, every time someone asked.

3

Now he uploads the general ledger export from the accounting system, same as always.

MarcSame columns as last month. The saved mapping does the rest.

4

Checks run before anything goes public.

  • It balances
  • It's the right period
  • No duplicate entries
  • No Social Security numbers or birth dates
5

Budget against actual, with the plow contract already counted as committed.

Budgeted$120,000
Committed$48,000
Paid so far$16,200
6

And the card charges?

Marc$200 of diesel on storm night. Card spend sits right next to the budget.

7

He publishes. The ledger gets its fingerprint on a public blockchain.

Published and fingerprinted

MarcNow anyone can check this file, including whoever asked.

8

Ten minutes later.

MarcUnder budget. Committed, paid, published. Here's the link.

A select board memberThat's it?

Same export. Checked, published, answered. Back to the list

The packet goes out on time

Sheila, Executive Administrative Assistant. Appointed, 11 years supporting the manager and the board.

JobGet a clean, correct, board-ready packet out on time, with no surprises she should have caught.

1

Thursday. The select board packet is due Friday at noon.

Tom, Town ManagerThe plow award is on the agenda. Is everything in the packet?

SheilaIt will be.

2

Last year, that meant calling the vendor for an insurance certificate. Twice.

3

This year, the vendor uploaded it when they registered.

SheilaInsurance certificate, on file, from the vendor's own account.

4

Proof the bid notice was posted?

SheilaA printable affidavit of posting. Done.

5

The board will ask how the winner was picked.

  • Bids opened in front of a witness
  • Evaluators signed conflict-of-interest statements
  • Scored blind against a set rubric
  • Reasons for the award on record
6

She downloads the contract's audit package in one click.

SheilaBids, scores, award and changes, all in one file.

7

Friday, 11:40 a.m.

Packet sent

SheilaTwenty minutes early, and nothing in there I should have caught.

8

Monday night. The board meeting.

A select board memberHow do we know nobody opened the bids early?

SheilaPage three.

Everything about the contract, in one file. Back to the list

Story 4 of 10 · Town Manager

No surprises at town meeting

Tom, Town Manager. Appointed, 4 years, answers to the select board.

JobWalk into every meeting able to say whether the town is on track, and never be blindsided by a number a resident found first.

1

Monday, 7:45 a.m. A message from the select board.

A select board memberPeople are talking about a 3 a.m. fuel charge on the plow contract. Do we know about this?

TomChecking now.

2

Before, he'd hear about it for the first time from a resident at the microphone.

3

Card spending publishes to the public ledger every day.

TomThere it is. $200 of diesel, the night of the storm.

4

He asks the published records a plain question.

AskedAre winter roads on budget?

AnswerYes. $48,000 is committed and $16,200 is paid, of $120,000.

5

The card was inside its limit, and staff can freeze it in an instant if they need to.

TomSo the controls did their job.

6

Three numbers, and one sentence of why.

Budgeted$120,000
Committed$48,000
Paid so far$16,200
7

Town meeting. Sam is at the microphone.

Sam, a residentWhat was the 3 a.m. fuel charge?

TomDiesel for the plows during the storm. It's on the town's records page, and you can check it yourself.

8

After the meeting.

TomNobody found a number before I did. That's the job.

The answer before the question. Back to the list

Story 5 of 10 · Treasurer and Tax Collector

My name is on the warrant

Linda, Treasurer and Tax Collector. Elected, part-time, 9 years, personally liable.

JobMake sure the money that left the account matches what was authorized, and be able to prove it.

1

Warrant day. The treasurer's office.

LindaNothing leaves the town's account unless I can tie it to an approval.

2

Last year, the approvals came in envelopes and the card receipts came in late.

3

The contractor claims milestone one. Staff approve it before any money moves.

LindaThe claim, the approval and the amount, on one record.

4

Paid by ACH, and tracked until it lands.

Milestone 1, by ACH$16,000
Payment statusCompleted
5

The storm-night fuel charge?

Linda$200 on the contract's card, inside its limit. I can freeze that card in an instant.

6

The funds were set aside the day the project was published.

LindaAnd I get a low-balance alert if that ever changes.

7

Month end. The bank balance register publishes with its own fingerprint on a public blockchain.

Matches what the town published

LindaAuthorized, paid and published. I can prove it.

8

Next warrant day.

LindaSame tie-out. No envelopes.

Authorized, paid, published. Back to the list

Story 6 of 10 · Purchasing Officer

An award that holds up

Ray, Purchasing Officer. Appointed, part-time, shared with Public Works, 7 years.

JobKeep spending inside awarded contracts, and make every award able to survive a challenge.

1

August. Public Works needs the roads plowed this winter.

Public WorksCan we just call the company we used last year?

RayWe bid it. And we bid it so nobody can say it went to somebody's cousin.

2

He starts from a template, not a blank page.

RayClauses for insurance and equipment, and state rules suggested for me.

3

Approved vendors are emailed the moment it opens.

RayIt's on the public listing, too, for anyone to follow.

4

Four bids arrive, each encrypted on the vendor's own device.

RayNobody can read them early. Not me, not Civic-Chain. Late bids are blocked.

5

Opening day.

  • Bids opened in front of a witness
  • Evaluators sign conflict-of-interest statements
  • Anonymous scores against a set rubric
  • Prices stay sealed until technical scores lock
6

The award goes out with its reasons on record.

Awarded$48,000
Backup vendorReady

RayAnd a backup vendor is ready if the winner falls through.

7

January. The contractor asks to add a route.

RayA contract change needs a second person's approval. That's on record, too.

8

The award is recorded on a public blockchain anyone can check.

RayIf anyone challenges this one, the record answers first.

The record answers first. Back to the list

JobCode every invoice correctly, pay on time, and survive the audit sample without scrambling for backup.

1

Tuesday. Accounts payable.

PriyaEvery invoice coded right, paid on time, and backed up for the audit sample.

2

Last year, invoices came by mail, and she matched each one to its contract by hand.

3

Now the contractor submits a claim for milestone one, inside the contract.

PriyaThe claim already knows its contract, its milestone and its amount.

4

Staff approve it. It pays by ACH, tracked to completion.

Contract$48,000
Paid so far$16,200
Left on contract$31,800
5

The storm-night fuel shows up on the plow contract's own card.

Priya$200 of diesel, already tied to the contract. No receipt hunt.

6

Her batch goes out as an accounts-payable export.

PriyaAnd at year end, the 1099 summary is ready.

Audit season. The auditor picks the plow contract as a sample.

Okafor, auditorBackup for this one?

PriyaOne download. The contract's whole audit package.

No scramble this year.

Story 9 of 10 · Independent Auditor

Evidence, not assertions

Okafor, Independent Auditor. Outside CPA firm, annual audit and interim fieldwork.

JobGather evidence efficiently, test that controls really work, and trace samples to their proof.

1

Interim fieldwork. A conference room at town hall.

OkaforDon't tell me the records are right. Show me.

2

Usually, that means days of pulling support out of file cabinets.

3

She picks a sample: the winter plowing contract.

OkaforOne download. Solicitation, bids, scores, award, changes and payments.

4

The activity log shows who did what, and when.

  • Bids opened in front of a witness
  • A second person approved the contract change
  • Every action logged
5

She follows the step-by-step instructions for independent auditors.

OkaforI'll check the published general ledger against its fingerprint myself.

6

The file hasn't changed since the day it was published.

Matches what the town published
7

And corrections?

OkaforA corrected version links to the original. Deleting a record takes two people and leaves a certificate. Nothing disappears quietly.

8

End of fieldwork.

OkaforLess time hunting for evidence. More time testing it.

Less hunting for evidence. More testing it. Back to the list

Story 10 of 10 · IT Coordinator and Records Manager

Who can see what

Dave, IT Coordinator and Records Manager. Contracted, part-time, covers several towns.

JobControl who can see and do what, keep the data secure and retained to schedule, and be able to get every record back out.

1

Dave covers IT for three towns. Today it's this one.

Ray, PurchasingCan our new purchasing clerk see the bids before they open?

DaveLet's look.

2

Drafting, opening bids, evaluating and awarding are separate rights.

DaveShe can draft. She can't open bids, and opening takes two people anyway.

3

Nobody can read a bid early. It's encrypted on the vendor's own device.

DaveNot staff, not me, not Civic-Chain.

4

Finance uploads a spreadsheet export. No new system to install.

DaveAnd the original file is deleted after import.

5

Before anything is published:

  • A scan for Social Security numbers and birth dates
  • Sensitive columns encrypted
  • Staff-only datasets stay staff-only
  • Only finance can publish, by default
6

What actually goes on the blockchain?

DaveA fingerprint. No money and no raw data.

7

Old bid files reach the end of their retention schedule.

DaveDisposal needs approval. Deleting a published record takes two people and leaves a certificate.

8

And if the town ever wants its data back out?

DavePublished records download in an open format, and contract history exports in the open-contracting standard.

Locked down, logged, and ours to keep. Back to the list
